background.text: Well, what could a poor rural boy do who was fairly vocal, but he didn't want to be a preacher? I mean, who used their speaking talents if they had whatever they had in that regard? How would you use them? I didn't want to be a preacher. I didn't want to be a teacher. And I never knew a lawyer. And I'd read some stories about great lawyers and thought that maybe that would be really fun to be a lawyer. So that's what happened.

background.speaker: SPEAKER_03
background.text: You know, I was wondering, you know, when you started out as a young lawyer, whether you regarded it as a job or as a life?

background.speaker: [target]
background.text: Well, it was an opportunity to feed my face and the face of my wife and the face of my children. I had one child and was another one on the way. So it was a means by which to make a living.

background.speaker: SPEAKER_03
background.text: At one point, actually, you decided to ditch the law and take up painting. What led to that, and how did that work out?

ground_truth: Well, the law, as I saw it at that time, was broken. And as I see it today, I still see that the justice system of this country is severely broken and does not offer anything except a promise, an empty promise to people of liberty and justice for all. It is not there. People can't get justice in this country. People believe that they can get justice until they need it, and then they can't get it. And I was about 38 years old. I had been in the law since I was 24 years old. I had accomplished about everything I could accomplish in this state. I had every verdict record in the state. I had the largest verdicts that people had ever heard of in this state. I'd never lost a criminal. I'd never been in a trial. And yet I wasn't getting, I wasn't providing, I was not providing justice. I couldn't provide justice. The system was wrong. And so what I thought to myself, what can I do with my life that would help this? And I thought, you know, maybe I'm a painter. I painted, began painting in my first marriage in the misery of my life. And I would paint out my misery, and I'd paint out my imaginations and my senses and my feelings. And the paintings were stacking up, and I got a great deal of pleasure from that and relief. And I thought, maybe I should become a painter, because I could teach people a lot about living through painting. Painting is nothing but a metaphor. Painting is nothing but a metaphor of life. Painting is nothing but a metaphor of life.
